stories.title: South Korea eases margin trading rules to curb forced stock sales
stories.summary: South Korean regulators loosened margin trading rules, aiming to reduce forced sales that occur when leveraged investors cannot meet margin calls. The move signals official concern about volatility tied to leveraged trading in the local market. The source does not detail the specific rule changes.
stories.whyItMatters: Forced selling from margin calls can amplify market swings, so this easing points to regulators trying to stabilize Korean equities.
whatToWatch: Market reaction in South Korean stocks after the change
Whether forced-sale volumes drop in coming sessions
questions: Which stocks or sectors faced the most forced selling?

stories.title: Doubleview Gold closes $3.2 million flow-through financing tranche

stories.title: Coca-Cola HBC says it has received no notification from Russia on asset changes
stories.summary: Bottler Coca-Cola HBC said it has not been notified of any changes regarding its assets in Russia, according to Investing.com. The statement comes amid continued scrutiny of Western companies' assets in Russia.
stories.whyItMatters: Western firms' Russian assets have faced seizure or forced-sale risk since the war began, so this update matters to investors assessing that exposure.
